heroHeadline: Day 387: India-Pakistan Military Chiefs Exchange Stark Warnings at Shangri-La Dialogue — CDS Chauhan Reaffirms Sindoor Doctrine; Gen. Mirza Warns Escalatory Threshold 'Dangerously Low'
heroSubtitle: June 1, 2026: The 23rd IISS Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore concluded with India's Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan and Pakistan's CJCSC General Sahir Shamshad Mirza delivering their sharpest public statements since Operation Sindoor. Chauhan: 'This operation lies in the military domain and should offer lessons to our adversary.' Mirza: 'The threshold of an escalatory war has come dangerously low' — calling for 'conflict resolution, not just management.' No bilateral India-Pakistan margins meeting occurred at the dialogue. The exchanges came one day after US DefSec Hegseth (May 31) endorsed Trump's ceasefire brokering claim at the same forum — India rejects external mediation; Pakistan amplifies it. Think Tank Journal analysis (June 1) identifies structural risks driving potential next confrontation: Kashmir, terrorism, China-Pakistan deepening, nuclear gray-zone, and military modernization surge. The ceasefire holds at Day 387 with no LOC violations since May 10, 2025. The bilateral freeze remains comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT suspended with India's 'null and void' PCA award rejection operative, Pakistan airspace ban through June 23/24, and four back-channel contacts as the only bilateral interaction.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
